inline_comments.comment: `buildModuleGraph` is included in the import from `./index`, but `index.ts` only *imports* it internally — it never re-exports it. This will produce a TypeScript compile error and the `buildModuleGraph` describe block will fail to run. The fix is to import `buildModuleGraph` directly from `'./utils/build-module-graph'` in the test instead.

`setInterval(async () => {...})` discards the Promise returned by the async callback. If `server.waitForRequestsIdle()` rejects, the error is silently swallowed — there is no catch path, no logging, and no way for listeners to learn that initialization failed. At minimum this should be wrapped in a try/catch that notifies listeners of the failure, or the async IIFE pattern `void (async () => { ... })()` should be used with proper error handling.

The polling interval has no upper bound. If `server.moduleGraph.fileToModulesMap.size` never exceeds 0 — for example due to a Vite configuration issue or an empty project — the interval will run indefinitely until `bail()` is called, but listeners will never receive an initial graph notification. A deadline (e.g. 30 seconds via `process.hrtime`) should stop the interval and signal an error to subscribers instead of silently looping forever.

The `if (!file) return undefined` early-return check occurs *before* the WeakMap lookup on line 37. Consider the case where a module with `file: null` is in `fileToModulesMap` and was already created using the `fallbackFile` argument (and stored in `moduleNodeMap`). When that same Vite node is later encountered as an importer or importedModule of a different node — without a fallback — the function returns `undefined` without consulting the WeakMap, causing the relationship to be silently dropped even though a valid node already exists. Moving the WeakMap check before the `!file` guard would fix this: if the node is already cached, return it regardless of whether a file can be resolved this time.

`notifyListeners` iterates over `listeners` with `forEach` but has no error boundary. If any listener callback throws, the `forEach` will propagate the exception up and all subsequent listeners in the Set will be silently skipped. This means one badly-behaved consumer can block all others from receiving the update. Wrap each call in a `try/catch` (logging and continuing) to make the notification loop resilient.

`bail()` silently clears all registered listeners. A consumer who subscribed via `onModuleGraphChange` before a server restart (bail + start) will have their subscription dropped with no indication — the returned `unsubscribe` handle becomes a no-op and the callback is never called again. This non-obvious contract should be documented on the `onModuleGraphChange` export (e.g. in a JSDoc comment noting that subscriptions do not survive `bail()` and must be re-registered after each restart).

`buildModuleGraph` reconstructs the entire module graph from scratch on every debounced watcher event. For large projects, the `fileToModulesMap` iteration combined with rebuilding full `importers`/`importedModules` Sets for every node could be expensive at the 100 ms debounce cadence. Consider whether an incremental or dirty-flagged approach is feasible, or whether the graph should only be rebuilt when the set of tracked files actually changes.

The `onModuleGraphChange` callback receives only a raw `ModuleGraph`, so the API has no way to signal transient states — for example, when the graph is still initializing, when Vite has restarted and the graph is temporarily stale, or when an error prevents graph construction. An event-envelope pattern (e.g. `{ type: 'moduleGraph', moduleGraph: ModuleGraph } | { type: 'error', error: Error } | { type: 'unavailable', reason: string }`) would be more extensible and prevent consumers from having to guess what an empty map means.

general_comments.comment: This PR adds four more module-level mutable variables (`listeners`, `debounce`, `watcherChangeHandler`, `waitForModuleGraph`) to `index.ts`, extending an already-present pattern with `server`. Module-level state makes the builder implicitly a singleton: multiple simultaneous instances (e.g. in a test suite that doesn't carefully call `bail()` between cases) will share and corrupt each other's state. Consider encapsulating all lifecycle state in a class or a factory function that returns a builder instance, which would make the ownership and cleanup surface explicit.

The `buildModuleGraph` function is a pure, independently testable utility, but its unit tests are placed in `index.test.ts` (the integration test file for the builder lifecycle) and the function is tested via an import that doesn't actually work (see the `./index` import defect above). Moving the `buildModuleGraph` tests into a dedicated `utils/build-module-graph.test.ts` file would improve discoverability, avoid the import issue, and keep the lifecycle tests focused on observable `start`/`bail`/`onModuleGraphChange` behavior.
